data.body:
RP25 false-positive experiment completed read-only on 2026-09-01 at snapshot 9a94ef9737fbdf070ae314bba6e797319aee2301. Baseline: `pytest -q tests/interfaces/contracts/test_no_sys_exit_in_read_core_176d.py` -> 9 passed in 0.79s. A one-off AST matcher covered sys.exit via module aliases, direct imported/builtin exit and quit, os._exit, and raised SystemExit (including aliases), excluding __main__ guards. Scope derived from CLI ROUTES read groups plus `_lib_reads`, `_lib_gates`, and `_mcp_reads` resolved to 12 production modules and produced 0 hits. The same matcher over all 620 `src/rebar` Python modules produced 12 hits, all intentional process owners: 9 CLI lifecycle exits, the Jira capability probe entrypoint, the test-pinned MCP missing-extra startup exit, and the ADR-0067 review-bot hard-shutdown seam. Thus there are no observed false positives in the intended current read scope, but a whole-tree rule would create 12.

A separate binding census found 0 current definitions/assignments shadowing exit, quit, SystemExit, or _exit; five sys/os module aliases exist but none invokes exit. RP25 should therefore require registry-derived scope, test-backed process-owner exclusions, import/lexical-binding resolution, and negative fixtures for shadowed exit/quit/SystemExit. The detailed commands, match rules, census, and classification are recorded in `.joe-janitor/tools.md`; the Remediation Plan entry records the result. RP25 remains pending approval.
